digest:
Recent work has pushed the frontier of holographic scattering by delivering the first worldsheet‑based two‑ and three‑point amplitudes for half‑BPS states in AdS$_5	imes$S$^5$ using a BRST‑invariant pure spinor prescription, reproducing planar $mathcal N=4$ SYM results and opening the door to higher‑point calculations.  In parallel, a Carrollian boundary description of massive scalars in flat space has been constructed, yielding explicit bulk‑to‑boundary transforms that encode mass through an infinite tower of primary states and provide a concrete bridge to celestial amplitudes via a free‑boson representation of electromagnetic memory correlators.  These developments dovetail with a nonabelianization map for $W_3$ conformal blocks, rewriting them in terms of Heisenberg blocks on a branched cover and confirming expected $	au$‑function behavior, thereby enriching the toolkit for higher‑point conformal block analysis.

On the algebraic side, Lie‑algebra cohomology of the $sl_2$ current algebra has been linked to the geometric Langlands program through a Poisson vertex algebra structure, while a study of rank‑two attractors in a mirror bicubic Calabi–Yau reveals modular $L$‑functions matching $ell$‑adic Galois representations—an explicit realization of arithmetic aspects of holography.  Meanwhile, Dirichlet walls in sinh‑dilaton gravity have been canonically quantized, producing $q$‑hypergeometric wavefunctions that identify the Hamiltonian with the reduced Casimir of $U_q(mathfrak{sl}(2,mathbb R))$, offering a quantum‑group interpretation reminiscent of Bruhat–Tits buildings.  Together, these papers weave a narrative that connects holographic amplitude techniques, celestial CFT, conformal block structures, and deep arithmetic and quantum‑group symmetries, aligning closely with the physicist’s interests in holography, celestial amplitudes, Langlands, and higher‑point conformal data.

papers.title: Horizon mergers and initial test-charge acceleration in charged black-hole geometries with anisotropic sources
papers.authors: Saeed Noori Gashti, Mohammad Ali S. Afshar, Mohammad Reza Alipour
papers.abstract: We study horizon mergers and the initial radial acceleration of charged test particles in static, spherically symmetric black-hole geometries with a string cloud, a Kiselev power-law component, or a logarithmic profile conventionally. After separating the Maxwell contribution, the effective environmental stress tensors are anisotropic and are not identified with homogeneous quintessence or pressureless cold dark matter. Using a common mass-function formulation, we derive the horizon-merger conditions and classify the Kiselev branches. In this family, the inner-event merger charge provides only an upper bound: three distinct positive horizons can additionally require a positive lower charge bound associated with the event-cosmological merger. For a test particle released from rest relative to a static observer, we derive the local charge-to-mass threshold for outward initial acceleration. Writing $\lambda=q/\mu$ and $z=Q/Q_{\rm ext}$, where $Q_{\rm ext}$ is the inner-event merger charge, the subextremal string-cloud threshold has infimum $1/z$, approached only at infinity. For the subextremal logarithmic profile, the threshold exceeds unity throughout the finite exterior and attains a finite global minimum. For $\alpha/M=0.4$ and $Q/M=1.2$, this minimum is $\lambda_*\simeq1.251125$. In a nondegenerate Kiselev static patch, the neutral balance radius is unique and radially unstable. Density matching supplies conditional profile normalizations, not observational fits. For the logarithmic profile, the integration parameter is distinguished from the mass combination inferred from circular motion. These results characterize geometric horizon bounds and test-particle dynamics; they do not establish a two-black-hole force law or a mechanism for cosmic acceleration, nor do they constitute a test of the Weak Gravity Conjecture.
papers.summary: The paper analyzes horizon mergers and initial acceleration of charged test particles in static, spherically symmetric black-hole spacetimes with anisotropic matter components, deriving horizon-merger conditions and charge-to-mass thresholds for outward acceleration. It finds that the thresholds depend on the specific anisotropic profile and provides explicit bounds, but does not address holographic or amplitude-related questions.

papers.title: Level repulsion and the quantum viscosity of near-extremal black branes
papers.authors: Panos Betzios, Olga Papadoulaki, Maria Myrto Pegioudi
papers.abstract: Below the gap scale of the AdS$_2$ throat, quantum fluctuations make the shear viscosity of near-extremal black branes grow as $(CT)^{-1/2}$ in the disk approximation of JT gravity, and the one-loop $\eta/s$ diverges. To cure this divergence, we include the non-perturbative completion of JT gravity as a matrix integral. The Kubo formula then probes universal features of level correlations. At finite extremal entropy $S_0$, level repulsion makes the DC viscosity vanish. A finite, universal viscosity survives in a double-scaling limit in which the probe frequency $\omega$ is held in a fixed ratio to the level-spacing scale $\omega_{\rm sp}\equiv e^{-S_0}/C$. At fixed $\omega$, with $\omega_{\rm sp}\ll\omega\ll e^{S_0/3}\omega_{\rm sp}$ the Schwarzian growth then saturates at $\eta_{\max}\simeq0.174\,(\omega/\omega_{\rm sp})\,\eta_{sc}$, where $\eta_{sc}$ is the semiclassical viscosity, and the viscosity decreases at lower temperatures. At the extremely low temperature scale $CT\sim e^{-2S_0/3}$ the genus expansion and the one-loop entropy computations completely break down. There we start probing the edge of the spectrum and the problem reduces exactly to the Airy kernel. We find that the ratio of the quenched averages of $\eta$ and $s$ is finite and positive at every non-zero temperature. We compare our results with explicit completions defined by the string equation, in which the spectrum is bounded from below. The bulk results are the same in these completions and the quenched edge results change only by a few per cent, while the annealed quantities depend on the non-perturbative completion at order one.
papers.summary: The paper studies how quantum fluctuations in the near‑extremal AdS$_2$ throat of black branes modify the shear viscosity, finding a $(CT)^{-1/2}$ growth and a divergent one‑loop $eta/s$ that is cured by a non‑perturbative matrix‑integral completion. In a double‑scaling limit the viscosity remains finite and universal, with level repulsion driving the DC viscosity to zero and the low‑temperature regime governed by the Airy kernel.

papers.title: The index from a super-point
papers.authors: Dhanvarsh Annamalai, Hyunook Hur, Thomas Hussel, Monica Jinwoo Kang, Craig Lawrie, Jaewon Song
papers.abstract: We extend the algebro-geometric construction of filtered graded rings that encode both the Higgs branch and the Macdonald index of 4d $\mathcal{N}=2$ superconformal field theories to theories whose Schur sector contains fermionic generators. The rings are then $\mathbb{Z}_2$-graded-commutative, and the index is reproduced by the Hilbert series of a generalized arc space, whose defining ideal may contain relations among the generators and their derivatives. We study the free $\mathcal{N}=2$ vector multiplet, $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang--Mills with gauge algebras $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ and $\mathfrak{su}(3)$, the rank-one $\mathcal{N}=3$ SCFTs, and the $\widehat{E}_6(SU(2))$ SCFT. For the rank-one $\mathcal{N}=3$ SCFTs, the ideal is the sum of the Jacobian ideals of a single superpotential and of its two supersymmetry variations. For $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang--Mills, the ideal is similarly the sum of the Jacobian ideals of the components of a single $\mathcal{N}=4$ superfield, which is a singlet of the $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ flavor symmetry for gauge algebra $\mathfrak{su}(2)$, and a triplet for $\mathfrak{su}(3)$. The associated VOA for the $\widehat{E}_6(SU(2))$ theory is given by the Feigin--Feigin--Tipunin $\mathcal{A}(6)$ algebra. The arc space of Zhu's $C_2$-algebra of $\mathcal{A}(6)$ does not reproduce the vacuum character, and therefore $\mathcal{A}(6)$ is not classically free. Supplementing Zhu's $C_2$-algebra by three relations in the first jet ring, the generalized arc space reproduces the Macdonald index of $\widehat{E}_6(SU(2))$ up to, at least, order $q^{51}$.
papers.summary: This work extends the algebraic construction of filtered graded rings encoding the Higgs branch and Macdonald index to theories with fermionic Schur sectors, introducing $mathbb{Z}_2$-graded-commutative rings and generalized arc spaces. It applies the framework to free vector multiplets, $mathcal{N}=4$ SYM, rank‑one $mathcal{N}=3$ SCFTs, and the $widehat{E}_6(SU(2))$ theory, reproducing their indices via Jacobian ideals and modified arc spaces.

papers.title: The Gradient Structure of Perturbative RG Flows
papers.authors: Lorenzo Benfatto, William H. Pannell, Andreas Stergiou
papers.abstract: Weyl consistency conditions show that perturbative renormalisation group flows in two, four and six dimensions are almost gradient flows. The obstruction is an antisymmetric contribution to the metric on the space of couplings, which has resisted removal since the work of Jack and Osborn more than 35 years ago. We show that a conformal Ward identity on the sphere allows it to be removed by a choice of scheme. The beta function is then the gradient of a potential $A$ with respect to a symmetric metric, to all orders in perturbation theory. The Ward identity gives this result in any dimension $d$, in theories with and without a Weyl anomaly. At leading order the metric is fixed by the two-point functions of the perturbing operators, so unitarity makes it positive definite at weak coupling. At fixed points $A$ equals $\widetilde{F}=\sin\tfrac{\pi d}{2}\,\ln Z_{S^{d}}$, so the $\widetilde{F}$-theorem follows for perturbative flows to all loop orders. We show that sources of relevant operators, which on the sphere mix with the curvature, do not affect these results. In unitary theories the only exception is the source of a free scalar field near $d=6,10,\ldots\,$, so that for $\phi^3$ theory near six dimensions the gradient property remains open.
papers.summary: The paper demonstrates that perturbative RG flows in two, four and six dimensions can be reformulated as true gradient flows by eliminating an antisymmetric obstruction through a conformal Ward identity on the sphere, yielding a symmetric metric and a potential A. At fixed points this potential equals the τF quantity, thereby extending the τF‑theorem to all loop orders in perturbation theory.

papers.title: An all-orders proof of gradient flow for multiscalar $\phi^4$ theory in four dimensions
papers.abstract: We prove that the renormalisation group flow of multiscalar $\phi^4$ theory in four dimensions is a gradient flow to all orders in perturbation theory. The proof uses the Weyl consistency conditions of Osborn and Jack, and it assumes two properties of perturbation theory: that the generating functional with local couplings is finite (also assumed by Osborn and Jack), and that the known expansion of massive Feynman integrals at large momenta holds with a bound on its remainder at each momentum. The consistency conditions give a gradient formula in which the tensor that multiplies the beta function is allowed to have an antisymmetric part, determined by coefficients of the Weyl anomaly. We derive a Ward identity for the two-point function of the marginal operators at constant couplings away from fixed points, with sources for the currents of field rotations and for the mass operator. It re-expresses one of the anti-symmetric contributions in terms of two-point functions and the first moment of the three-point function. We show that, after this rewrite, each of the resulting terms is equivalent to a symmetric contribution to the metric and a contribution to the potential, and we give both explicitly. The metric is positive definite to all orders in perturbation theory. The proof implies in particular the four relations among five- and six-loop coefficients of the field rotation, which Pannell and Stergiou derived as the conditions for a gradient flow at six loops. We check by explicit computation that these relations indeed hold. A companion paper treats $d=4-\varepsilon$ and other critical dimensions with a Ward identity on the sphere.
papers.summary: The paper proves that the renormalisation group flow of multiscalar φ⁴ theory in four dimensions is a gradient flow to all orders in perturbation theory, using Weyl consistency conditions and assumptions about finiteness of the generating functional with local couplings and the large‑momentum expansion of massive Feynman integrals. It derives a Ward identity for two‑point functions of marginal operators, rewrites antisymmetric contributions into symmetric metric and potential terms, and confirms the resulting metric is positive definite, thereby verifying six‑loop gradient flow conditions.

papers.title: Bring Your Own Instanton: Monopole Catalysis from Sourced SU(2) Instantons
papers.authors: Csaba Cs\'aki, Larissa Kiriliuk, Zhihan Liu, Rotem Ovadia
papers.abstract: We show that Rubakov-Callan catalysis of proton decay in the field of a 't Hooft-Polyakov monopole proceeds through "sourced SU(2) instantons", which are novel topological gauge configurations sourced by fermions and carrying unit instanton number. Unlike vacuum BPST instantons, these sourced instantons do not give rise to exponentially suppressed rates. We relate the winding number to the number of fermionic zero modes, suggesting an underlying index theorem for sourced instantons. We also calculate the closed-form expression for the leading-order correlator for fermion insertions both outside and inside the monopole core. Our results indicate that Rubakov-Callan catalysis is an IR effect where the scattering fermions do not reach the monopole core.
papers.summary: The authors introduce ‘sourced SU(2) instantons’—fermion‑generated gauge configurations with unit instanton number that mediate Rubakov‑Callan proton decay without exponential suppression. They compute the leading‑order fermion correlator inside and outside the monopole core, showing the catalysis is an IR effect and suggesting an index theorem for these instantons.

papers.title: Wormholes do not contribute to supersymmetric partition functions
papers.abstract: We show that wormholes connecting multiple asymptotic boundaries always spontaneously break at least some of the symmetries preserved by their boundary conditions. Their configurations then form nontrivial orbits of the broken symmetry, and for the case of a fermionic symmetry, the contribution of each orbit vanishes. We conclude that wormholes do not contribute to moments of supersymmetric partition functions. This extends results on supersymmetric indices by Iliesiu, Kologlu, and Turiaci. We emphasize that supersymmetric partition functions can still have a nonzero ensemble variance. In SYK-like examples that we analyze, this arises due to the contribution of ``non-geometric wormhole'' configurations that preserve all continuous symmetries.
papers.summary: The authors prove that any wormhole connecting multiple asymptotic boundaries spontaneously breaks at least one of the symmetries preserved by the boundary conditions, and for fermionic symmetries the resulting orbit contributions cancel, implying that such wormholes do not contribute to supersymmetric partition functions. Nevertheless, they show that ensemble variance can still be nonzero due to non‑geometric wormhole configurations that preserve all continuous symmetries in SYK‑like models.

papers.title: The chiral $M^{3,2}$ theory: partition functions beyond large-$N$ and quantum holography
papers.abstract: We identify families of Bethe vacua in the chiral $M^{3,2}$ theory whose individual free energies grow as $N^{3/2}$. High-precision data support closed forms for their all-order perturbative $1/N$ expansions. At a distinguished mixed Chern--Simons coupling, the baryonic magnetic flux distinguishes members of this family of vacua. We also study the three-sphere partition function numerically in the 't Hooft limit and Cardy limit, and propose an all-order Airy formula. The four-derivative and one-loop corrections are precision tests of holography.
papers.summary: The paper studies Bethe vacua of the chiral M^{3,2} theory, finding that their free energies scale as N^{3/2} and exhibit closed-form 1/N expansions. It also numerically analyzes the three-sphere partition function in various limits, proposing an all-order Airy formula that tests quantum holography via higher-derivative and one-loop corrections.

papers.title: Relativistic Hydrodynamics as an Intersection Problem
papers.abstract: Ideal relativistic hydrodynamics admits a covariant description as an intersection problem in a symplectic space associated with spacetime. The independent fields are differential forms of degrees 0,1,3,4. Spacetime diffeomorphisms and shifts of the momentum one-form act Hamiltonianly; the zero locus of their moment map is a coisotropic subvariety encoding the transport equations. The spacetime metric and equation of state determine a Lagrangian submanifold, whose intersection with the coisotropic subvariety is precisely the Lichnerowicz--Carter system. We explain the geometric meaning of the canonical flow parameter, derive circulation and Ertel invariants directly from the constraints, and identify energy--momentum conservation with covariance of the constitutive Lagrangian. The nonrelativistic limit and a relation of entropy-level helicity to split Calabi--Yau geometry are briefly indicated.
papers.summary: The paper reformulates ideal relativistic hydrodynamics as a symplectic intersection problem, identifying the transport equations with the zero locus of a moment map and the Lichnerowicz–Carter system as the intersection with a Lagrangian submanifold. It further derives circulation and Ertel invariants from the constraints and discusses a split Calabi–Yau interpretation of entropy-level helicity in the nonrelativistic limit.

papers.title: Massive Particles in Carrollian Holography
papers.authors: Bin Chen, Zezhou Hu, Reiko Liu, Wen-Jie Ma
papers.abstract: Understanding how massive particles are encoded in boundary operators is a central problem in Carrollian holography. We construct a three-dimensional Carrollian description of a massive scalar in four-dimensional flat spacetime, together with an explicit bulk-to-boundary integral transform. In this construction, nonzero mass requires infinitely many linearly independent primary states, while the absence of bulk spin imposes relations among their descendants. We show that these relations are equivalent to null-state decoupling and give a local constraint on the boundary fields. The integral transform preserves the full Poincar\'e symmetry and maps bulk scalar data to fields satisfying this constraint. We also obtain two- and three-point functions and the associated formal operator product expansion coefficients. The integral transform evaluates bulk data at complex momenta, making analytic continuation essential in Lorentzian signature. This construction provides a concrete starting point for relating massive scattering amplitudes to Carrollian correlators and for reconstructing bulk fields from boundary data.
papers.summary: This work constructs a Carrollian boundary description of a massive scalar in 4D flat spacetime, deriving an explicit bulk-to-boundary integral transform that preserves Poincaré symmetry and encodes mass via infinitely many primary states linked by null-state decoupling. The authors compute two- and three-point functions, giving a concrete bridge between massive scattering amplitudes and Carrollian correlators, and lay groundwork for reconstructing bulk fields from boundary data.

papers.title: Thermodynamics of hard wall model of AdS/QCD at finite chemical potential with Gauss-Bonnet corrections
papers.abstract: We study the confinement/deconfinement transition of the hard wall model of AdS/QCD at finite quark density in five-dimensional Einstein--Maxwell--Gauss--Bonnet gravity, with the back-reaction of the quark matter on the geometry included. The deconfined phase is a charged Gauss--Bonnet black hole, and the confined phase is thermally charged AdS cut off in the infrared. The infrared value of the gauge field, which Lee, Park and Sin fixed by requiring a consistent quark number, becomes a function of the Gauss--Bonnet coupling. We obtain the transition line in closed form at fixed quark chemical potential and at fixed quark number density. At fixed density the transition passes through a region where the two phases coexist. A negative Gauss--Bonnet coupling raises the transition temperature and extends the confined phase to higher density. A value inside the causality bound gives a transition temperature at zero density close to the lattice value. In the dense confined phase we compute the masses and decay constants of the $\rho$ meson and its radial excitations. All masses increase with density. A WKB analysis relates the increase to a shorter effective size of the confining region, and at nuclear density the $\rho$ mass rises by about one percent.
papers.summary: The authors analyze the confinement/deconfinement transition in a hard-wall AdS/QCD model with finite quark density, incorporating back-reaction via Einstein–Maxwell–Gauss–Bonnet gravity. They derive a closed-form phase diagram, show how a negative Gauss–Bonnet coupling raises the transition temperature, and compute density-dependent rho-meson spectra.

papers.title: Finite-Temperature Stabilization of a KKLT Modulus in Three-Dimensional Lattice Simulations
papers.authors: Saya Mahmoudi, Furkan Utku Biber, Hyukjung Kim, Heeseung Zoe
papers.abstract: We investigate the cosmological stabilization of a KKLT modulus through three-dimensional Langevin lattice simulations incorporating an evolving thermal bath, dissipation, spatial gradients, and stochastic fluctuations. While the spatially averaged modulus closely follows homogeneous evolution away from the capture threshold, near-critical trajectories linger near the unstable potential barrier for approximately one e-fold, allowing long-wavelength fluctuations to undergo tachyonic amplification and drive localized regions across the barrier even as the mean field turns back toward the stabilized vacuum. Linear Langevin theory reproduces the fluctuation growth, while convergence tests identify a narrow stochastic layer in which the barrier-crossing fraction shows no systematic dependence on the discretization at a fixed effective distance from the threshold. These results demonstrate that capture of the spatially averaged modulus does not guarantee that every spatial region remains within the stabilizing barrier.
papers.summary: The study uses three‑dimensional Langevin lattice simulations to follow a KKLT modulus in a thermal bath, revealing that while the spatial average can be captured by the stabilizing potential, local regions can escape the barrier due to tachyonic amplification of long‑wavelength fluctuations. It demonstrates that global capture does not guarantee local stability, highlighting the importance of stochastic effects in modulus dynamics.

papers.title: Exact stress-tensor fluctuations from conformal symmetry and black hole radiation
papers.authors: Jos\'e Navarro-Salas, Roberto Balbinot, Alessandro Fabbri
papers.abstract: Semiclassical gravity is sourced by the expectation value of the stress tensor, and it is reliable only if the fluctuations around this value are small. In two dimensions, conformal symmetry captures the essential physics of Hawking radiation in its s-wave sector and determines the mean value exactly, for any background and any quantum state. We show that it also determines the local fluctuations of the null components $T_{\pm\pm}$. The square of the stress tensor is defined by the operator product expansion, up to a multiple $\alpha$ of $\partial_\pm^2T_{\pm\pm}$ that labels point-splitting prescriptions. Its transformation law under the conformal map to locally inertial coordinates gives the variance in closed form. The relative fluctuation scales as $1/c$, with $c$ the central charge. For the Schwarzschild black hole it is $22/5c$ for the Hawking flux at infinity, that of flat-space thermal radiation. At the horizon it is $-44\alpha/3c$ for the outgoing flux and $(238+720\alpha)/5c$ for the ingoing flux that drives the backreaction. Both reduce to $22/5c$ for $\alpha=-3/10$, which corresponds to the M\"obius-covariant prescription. For large $c$ these results support the semiclassical approximation.
papers.summary: This paper shows that in 2D CFT the conformal symmetry fixes not only the mean stress tensor but also its local fluctuations, giving explicit variance formulas for Hawking flux in Schwarzschild geometry. The results confirm that for large central charge the semiclassical approximation remains valid, with the variance scaling as 1/c and a specific point‑splitting parameter α fixing the M"obius‑covariant prescription.

papers.title: The Generalized Second Law from Fluctuation Theorems in a Quantum Reference Frame
papers.abstract: We prove the generalized second law (GSL) for black-hole exteriors undergoing unitary driving and relaxation on a fixed semifinite algebra. Wall's influential proof assumes semiclassical geometry and restricts fixed parent states to algebras of successive horizon cuts. We instead evolve the state on a fixed dressed exterior algebra. With complete characteristic data, the same semiclassical exterior supports both descriptions, analogous to the Heisenberg and Schr\"odinger pictures through state--operator duality. Using a gravitational charge as a quantum clock, we construct a modular crossed product with density operators whose trace entropy reproduces generalized entropy up to clock contributions. Our approach parallels thermodynamics in regulated field theory and formulates the GSL through a quantum channel fluctuation theorem (FT) for the open exterior. We develop three complementary formulations under specified dynamical assumptions. Separated unitary driving and relaxation combine modular work, the physical-process first law relating horizon absorption to area gain, and relative-entropy contraction through data processing. A time-local description accommodates simultaneous unitary driving and dissipation. A two-time surprisal FT treats the complete channel, identifies the nonunital correction, and yields a GSL bound for unital dressed evolution without resolving intermediate dynamics. Relaxation that does not mix distinct dressed-charge sectors and preserves the full dressed reference state is unital. Unitality is sufficient for this FT proof but is not necessary for the GSL along a particular evolution. The entropy bounds establish the GSL in a controlled slow-clock limit and quantify finite-width clock corrections.
papers.summary: The paper extends Wall’s proof of the generalized second law to a fixed dressed exterior algebra by employing modular crossed products and a quantum channel fluctuation theorem. It shows that unitary driving and relaxation on a semiclassical background satisfy a GSL bound, with finite-width clock corrections quantified in a slow-clock limit.

papers.title: Symmetry resolved spread complexity for BMN matrix model
papers.abstract: We investigate the symmetry-resolved spread complexity of the Berenstein-Maldacena-Nastase (BMN) matrix model under a global $U(1)$ symmetry acting within the transverse $SO(6)$ scalar sector. Decomposing the time-evolved charged thermofield double (cTFD) state into orthogonal fixed-charge sectors, we examine the return amplitude, spectral moments, tridiagonal Lanczos coefficients, and early-time spread complexity across the low-temperature confined ($\beta\mu \gg 1$) and finite-temperature deconfined ($T \gg \mu$) phases. In the low-temperature gapped regime, effective sector dynamics map onto decoupled, displaced harmonic oscillators with a Casimir-like zero-point offset, yielding factorized moments, linear drift in diagonal Lanczos coefficients $a_n^{(q)}$, and sub-linear $\sqrt{n}$ off-diagonal growth with thermally suppressed initial hopping. Charge-dependent Boltzmann weights, vacuum shifts, and degeneracies break complexity equipartition, while inter-sector coherence and charge dispersion enforce an early-time positivity bound $\Delta C(t) = C_{\text{total}}(t) - \bar{C}(t) \ge 0$. In the \emph{finite}-temperature continuum phase, modeling the planar large-$N$ spectral density as a thermal Gaussian gives constant diagonal coefficients $a_n^{(q)} = \bar{E}_q$, universal square-root scaling $b_n^{(q)} = \sigma_E \sqrt{n}$, and a quadratic spread launch $\mathcal{C}^{(q)}(t) = \sigma_E^2(q,T)\,t^2 + \mathcal{O}(t^4)$ governed by the backreacted sector energy variance. Holographically, these regimes distinguish coherent string fluctuations in horizonless Lin-Maldacena (LM) droplet geometries from dissipative scrambling near charged ten-dimensional black D0-brane horizons.
papers.summary: This work studies symmetry-resolved spread complexity in the BMN matrix model, analyzing charged thermofield double dynamics in confined and deconfined phases. It connects the results to holographic duals, distinguishing coherent string fluctuations in Lin-Maldacena geometries from scrambling near charged D0-brane horizons.

papers.title: Scattering amplitudes in AdS$_5\times$ S$^5$ from the pure spinor superstring
papers.authors: Luis F. Alday, Thiago Fleury, Tobias Hansen, Lucas N. S. Martins, Dennis Zavaleta
papers.abstract: We formulate a BRST-invariant prescription for the integration of zero modes in the pure spinor superstring on $AdS_5\times S^5$. The measure includes contributions absent in flat space and admits a description in terms of picture changing operators or a non-minimal regulator. The prescription is valid for genus-zero amplitudes with arbitrary multiplicity and external states and removes a central obstacle to amplitude computations in this background. We use it to perform the first direct worldsheet computation of two and three-point amplitudes of half-BPS supergravity states. The properly normalised three-point amplitudes exactly reproduce the results of planar ${\mathcal N}=4$ super Yang-Mills theory.
papers.summary: The paper develops a BRST‑invariant method for integrating zero modes in the pure spinor superstring on AdS$_5	imes S^5$, enabling genus‑zero amplitude calculations for any number of external states. Using this prescription, the authors compute the first direct worldsheet two‑ and three‑point amplitudes of half‑BPS supergravity states, finding perfect agreement with planar $mathcal N=4$ SYM results.

papers.title: Quadratic-in-spin scattering of compact bodies at fourth post-Minkowskian order
papers.abstract: We present the fourth-post-Minkowskian scattering angle of aligned spinning compact bodies through quadratic spin at arbitrary velocity and mass ratio. We include spin-induced quadrupoles and radiation reaction, supplemented by curvature-squared spin-tidal terms. Three-loop worldline integrals yield closed forms in polylogarithms and elliptic integrals. Infrared poles cancel exactly, fixing the tail logarithm. We obtain a new post-Newtonian coefficient and third-order angular-momentum loss for general quadrupoles. The new input shifts resummed predictions for black-hole scattering.
papers.summary: The paper computes the fourth-post-Minkowskian scattering angle for aligned spinning compact bodies, including quadratic spin effects, spin-induced quadrupoles, and radiation reaction, using three-loop worldline integrals that yield closed forms in polylogarithms and elliptic integrals. It also provides new post-Newtonian coefficients and angular-momentum loss terms, refining resummed predictions for black-hole scattering.

papers.title: A note on Holographic Renormalization for Polarized IKKT
papers.abstract: We construct a boundary counterterm for the on-shell action of type IIB supergravity solutions dual to vacua of the polarized IKKT matrix model. The construction is based on the variational principle, with off-shell fluctuations whose fall-off conditions are based on the asymptotic equations of motion. The renormalized on-shell action of the supersymmetric saddles reproduces the matrix- model result once we pass to the ensemble of fixed D1-brane charges, which we implement off-shell by dualizing the RR two-form potential.
papers.summary: The paper presents a boundary counterterm that renders the on‑shell action of type IIB supergravity dual to polarized IKKT vacua finite, using a variational principle with asymptotic fall‑off conditions derived from the equations of motion. The resulting renormalized action matches the matrix‑model prediction when the D1‑brane charge is fixed via dualization of the RR two‑form, providing a holographic check of the polarized IKKT construction.

papers.title: Infrared finite scattering theory: Non-relativistic Coulomb scattering
papers.abstract: We revisit non-relativistic quantum-mechanical scattering in a Coulomb potential. The long-range nature of the interaction leads to divergent integrals in conventional S-matrix calculations using the Born series. Dollard showed that a well-defined scattering operator can be constructed by replacing the free Hamiltonian $ H_0 $ with an appropriate asymptotic Hamiltonian $ H_{\rm D} $. However, explicit perturbative calculations within Dollard's framework have remained scarce. We develop a perturbative formulation of the Dollard scattering operator in which the Coulomb divergences cancel to all orders. Perturbatively, we demonstrate this cancellation explicitly through second Born order and show that the resulting amplitude reproduces the known exact distributional Coulomb amplitude, including its forward-scattering contribution. With the aim of generalizing our analysis to quantum field theory, we reformulate the problem in the Heisenberg picture. We construct a new set of canonical variables through a time-dependent canonical transformation that removes the logarithmic Coulomb correction from the asymptotic phase-space coordinates. Using these variables, we construct the corresponding Heisenberg S-matrix through several complementary approaches. This leads to a formulation of the Lehmann--Symanzik--Zimmermann (LSZ) reduction formalism adapted to the modified asymptotic dynamics, which we relate to the Dollard scattering operator. This construction provides a framework for extending the LSZ formalism to infrared divergences in relativistic quantum field theories with long-range interactions and massless fields.
papers.summary: This work develops a perturbative Dollard scattering operator that cancels Coulomb divergences to all orders, reproducing the exact Coulomb amplitude including forward scattering. It also reformulates the problem in the Heisenberg picture, introducing time-dependent canonical variables and an LSZ-like reduction adapted to long-range dynamics, laying groundwork for handling infrared divergences in relativistic QFT.

papers.title: Bounds on entanglement fluctuations at holographic interfaces
papers.abstract: How small can entanglement fluctuations be at fixed entropy? For a class of holographic conformal interfaces supported by a scalar with a potential, we prove $c_\text{eff}\leq c_\text{cap}\leq c_\text{eff}^2/c_{LR}$, relating entropy, capacity, and energy transmission. The coupled gravitational response is a transport term minus a positive scalar contribution; the background Einstein equation bounds that subtraction. A long Janus throat allows unbounded capacity at a finite entropy coefficient while the scalar response remains gapped.
papers.summary: The paper investigates how small entanglement fluctuations can be for a fixed entropy in holographic conformal interfaces, deriving bounds that relate entropy, capacity, and energy transmission via a scalar field. It shows that a long Janus throat can yield unbounded capacity at finite entropy while keeping the scalar response gapped, offering new insights into transport in holographic systems.

papers.title: Lie Algebra Cohomology and Seiberg-Witten Theory
papers.abstract: We compute the algebra of perturbative holomorphic-topological local operators of pure $\mathcal N=2$ gauge theory with gauge group $SU(2)$, proving a conjecture of the author: it is the Poisson vertex algebra generated by a Virasoro element $X$ of central charge zero and an odd primary $Y$ of weight three, subject only to $X^2=0$. Equivalently, we compute the relative Lie algebra cohomology $H^*(\mathfrak{sl}_2[z,w]/(w^2),\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ and the self-Ext groups of the unit in the coherent Satake category for $SL_2$ and $PGL_2$. The proof uses factorization on configuration spaces of points on the affine line, a depth argument, and two deformations of the coefficient algebra $\mathbb C[z,w]/(w^2)$.
papers.summary: We compute the algebra of perturbative holomorphic‑topological local operators in pure N=2 SU(2) gauge theory, showing it is a Poisson vertex algebra generated by a Virasoro element and an odd primary subject only to X^2=0. This result is equivalent to determining the relative Lie algebra cohomology H^*(sl_2[z,w]/(w^2),sl_2) and the self‑Ext groups of the unit in the coherent Satake category, linking gauge theory to geometric Langlands via factorization on configuration spaces.

papers.title: Boundary spectroscopy of hidden near-horizon reflection
papers.authors: Yiling Chen, Jiayue Yang, Zhen Zhong, Robert B. Mann, Jie Jiang, Ming Zhang
papers.abstract: A classical black hole horizon absorbs completely, and any deviation would be hidden in the bulk. For a scalar field in a rotating Ba\~nados-Teitelboim-Zanelli exterior, we derive an exact boundary response of a corotating passive wall near the horizon. An Airy filter gives its spectrum, and positive energy excludes growing modes. On any frequency band the response identifies a constant wall impedance and the wall position, which enter orthogonally with weights determined by the spectral function. The boundary thus sees a reflecting wall, whereas a perfect absorber is exponentially hidden.
papers.summary: The paper derives an exact boundary response for a scalar field in a rotating BTZ background, revealing a hidden reflecting wall near the horizon. It shows that the wall’s impedance and position can be extracted from the spectrum, providing a holographic probe of near-horizon physics.

papers.title: Charged spin-$\frac32$ in a chiral Feshbach--Villars model: hyperbolic propagation, Landau-level instability, and exceptional points
papers.abstract: We study a Pauli-coupled second-order wave equation on $(\frac32,0)\oplus(0,\frac32)$ with a free gyromagnetic ratio $g$. Its Feshbach--Villars form is a sixteen-component pseudo-Hermitian Hamiltonian system with lightlike covariant characteristics in smooth electromagnetic backgrounds. The solution space is chirality doubled; a covariant physical single-species reduction is not assumed. The exact spin-$j$ Landau spectrum remains real at every field strength precisely when $|g|j\le1$. At $g=2$, the critical spin-$\frac32$ channel reaches zero at $|qB|=m^2/2$, where each chiral block develops a second-order exceptional point. This threshold also marks the loss of a time-independent positive-definite conserved quadratic form for the channel. We also include a bounded, Gaussian-damped harmonic electrostatic potential and its associated electric field. The complete first-order problem on a degenerate manifold reduces to $V\pm iC$, with $V$ and $C$ the projected potential and spin--electric coupling. On the lowest two-state spin-$\frac32$ manifold, nonreal eigenvalue branches arise for $m^2/6<|qB|<m^2/2$ at sufficiently small nonzero perturbation amplitude, except at a special well range where the first-order splitting vanishes. The spin-$\frac12$, $g=2$ limit satisfies the Dirac spectral-reality check, whereas $g=1/j$ has no imaginary first-order correction for this perturbation. These results separate spectral instability from loss of hyperbolicity; they do not establish a physical fermionic quantization.
papers.summary: The paper investigates a second‑order wave equation for a charged spin‑3/2 field coupled to electromagnetism, deriving a sixteen‑component pseudo‑Hermitian Hamiltonian and analyzing its Landau‑level spectrum, exceptional points, and spectral stability under electric perturbations. It finds that the spectrum remains real only for |g|j≤1, with a critical g=2 spin‑3/2 mode becoming unstable at |qB|=m^2/2, but does not connect to known holographic or conformal field theory frameworks.

papers.title: Matter-decorated trumpets in double-scaled SYK
papers.abstract: In sine-dilaton gravity, the double trumpet, the wormhole amplitude without matter, is obtained by gluing two trumpets along a closed geodesic of discrete length and summing over this length. When the wormhole carries the propagator of a matter field of dimension $\Delta$, joining the two asymptotic boundaries and crossing the neck, such a gluing is known only in the Jackiw--Teitelboim (JT) limit. We construct the gluing beyond JT in double-scaled SYK (DSSYK), the proposed boundary dual of sine-dilaton gravity, whose disk amplitudes it reproduces. In this context, we adopt the definition of the matter-decorated wormhole in terms of the ETH two-matrix model with Gaussian matter. We build matter-decorated trumpets from an end-of-the-world brane trace with a matter insertion, and prove that the wormhole is glued from them exactly, sector by sector in the number of chords through the neck, with a positive weight that accounts for the twists and windings of these chords and for the closed loops around the neck. Trumpets and weight are obtained in closed form, the former as transforms of Rogers polynomials, and we discuss the uniqueness of the construction. In the JT limit, both reproduce the known gluing separately, and not only in combination. In the classical limit, each trumpet takes the form expected in the bulk: a pure-gravity sine-dilaton trumpet dressed by the factor that a probe matter geodesic contributes at its boundary.
papers.summary: The paper constructs a matter‑decorated double‑trumpet wormhole in double‑scaled SYK, extending the known JT gluing to a full sine‑dilaton gravity dual. It uses an ETH two‑matrix model with Gaussian matter to build trumpets from end‑of‑the‑world brane traces, proving exact sector‑by‑sector gluing with positive weights that encode chord twists and windings.

papers.title: Rotating Black Holes from Scaling Transformations in Horava Gravity
papers.abstract: We study the scaling transformations that change the physical parameters of solutions in low-energy Horava gravity. In particular, we present a simple scaling transformation that generates rotating black-hole solutions in low-energy Horava gravity from known relativistic solutions. As explicit examples, we obtain "Doran-like" and "Kerr-Schild-like" rotating solutions in Horava gravity. We find that both solutions are horizon-penetrating, but their null horizons are not Killing horizons. We also find that, although their singularity structures differ from each other, chronology is protected in both solutions, as in the previously obtained Kerr-like solutions in Boyer-Lindquist coordinates.
papers.summary: This work constructs rotating black-hole solutions in low-energy Horava gravity by applying a simple scaling transformation to known relativistic metrics, yielding Doran-like and Kerr–Schild-like geometries that are horizon-penetrating but possess non‑Killing null horizons. The authors show that despite differing singularity structures, both spacetimes maintain chronology protection, extending previous Kerr-like results.

papers.title: Darboux transformation for the ASDYM equations: Solitons and instantons
papers.abstract: Using a one-fold Darboux transformation for the anti-self-dual Yang--Mills equations, we express the Yang--Mills Lagrangian density in terms of $\tau$-functions. For solitons constructed from exponential functions, we show that the associated $\tau$-functions admit a parametrization by arbitrary points in the Grassmannian Gr(N,M;$\mathbb{C}$), and construct the corresponding Yang--Mills fields. For instantons arising from the Atiyah--Drinfeld--Hitchin--Manin (ADHM) construction, we reinterpret the ADHM construction in terms of a one-fold Darboux transformation, recover Osborn's formula for the Yang--Mills Lagrangian density, and obtain the corresponding gauge connection.
papers.summary: This paper develops a one‑fold Darboux transformation for the anti‑self‑dual Yang–Mills equations, expressing the Yang–Mills Lagrangian in terms of τ‑functions and linking soliton solutions to points in the Grassmannian. It also reinterprets the ADHM instanton construction as a Darboux transformation, reproducing Osborn’s formula for the Lagrangian density and constructing the corresponding gauge connection.

papers.title: Non-invertible Duality Defects in Four-Dimensional $\mathbb{Z}_N$ Lattice Gauge Theories
papers.abstract: We consider four-dimensional $\mathbb{Z}_N$ lattice gauge theories with generalized plaquette actions. These theories are known to exhibit dualities. We construct topological interfaces implementing these dualities by assigning a weight to each building block and proving topological invariance. At self-dual couplings, these interfaces become duality defects representing non-invertible symmetries. We also study center symmetry defects and their junctions with the duality interfaces and derive several crossing relations.
papers.summary: This paper constructs topological interfaces in 4d [Z_N] lattice gauge theories that implement duality transformations, showing that at self‑dual couplings these interfaces become non‑invertible duality defects. The authors also analyze center symmetry defects, their junctions with the duality interfaces, and derive crossing relations among them.

papers.title: Dirichlet walls beyond JT gravity and their quantum group interpretation
papers.authors: Luca Griguolo, Jacopo Papalini, Lorenzo Russo, Domenico Seminara, Alex Tarana
papers.abstract: We canonically quantize sinh dilaton gravity with finite Dirichlet boundary conditions. The reduced phase space is formulated in terms of the length of a two-sided spacelike geodesic in an effective AdS$_2$ geometry and its conjugate momentum. Canonical quantization leads to a finite-difference Schr\"odinger equation whose wavefunctions of the universe are given by $q$-hypergeometric functions. These furnish a quantum deformation of the hypergeometric wavefunctions of JT gravity. We further show that the finite cutoff Hamiltonian derived from the bulk analysis admits a natural interpretation as the reduced Casimir of $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{R}))$ acting on hyperbolic matrix elements. The two scattering wave solutions are hyperbolic matrix elements of the modular double $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb R))\otimes U_{\tilde q}(\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb R))$, and the wavefunction of the universe is their unique combination regular at vanishing length.
papers.summary: This paper canonically quantizes sinh‑dilaton gravity with finite Dirichlet boundaries, producing a finite‑difference Schrödinger equation whose solutions are q‑hypergeometric functions that deform the JT gravity wavefunctions. The Hamiltonian is identified with the reduced Casimir of the quantum group (U_q(mathfrak{sl}(2,mathbb{R}))), and the scattering states are hyperbolic matrix elements of the modular double, giving a quantum‑group interpretation of AdS(_2) dynamics.

papers.title: Conservative tidal effects to third post-Minkowskian order in scalar-tensor theories
papers.abstract: Using worldline effective field theory, we compute the conservative finite-size contributions to the impulse and scattering angle of nonspinning compact binaries in massless scalar-tensor theories with a scalar-Gauss-Bonnet coupling through third post-Minkowskian (3PM) order. We retain the full velocity dependence at linear order in the tidal response coefficients. The calculation covers the scalar dipole and quadrupole and the electric, magnetic, and mixed quadrupoles and octupoles. Among them, the scalar dipole enters the dynamics already at third post-Newtonian (3PN) order, two orders before the gravitational quadrupole. At 3PM, the tidal correction to the angle also depends on the first scalar derivatives of the responses and contains terms linear in the Gauss-Bonnet coupling. The results reproduce the general-relativistic tidal angle and the post-Newtonian tidal dynamics through 5PN, and a test-body calculation confirms their leading order in the mass ratio, including the Gauss-Bonnet terms for a companion with vanishing sensitivity.
papers.summary: This paper computes third‑post‑Minkowskian tidal corrections for non‑spinning binaries in massless scalar‑tensor theories, including scalar‑Gauss‑Bonnet couplings and full velocity dependence at linear order in tidal response coefficients. The results recover known general‑relativistic tidal angles and PN dynamics up to 5PN, and confirm the leading mass‑ratio limit via a test‑body calculation.

papers.title: Gradient formula from the sphere for perturbative RG flows near critical dimensions
papers.abstract: We study the gradient property of perturbative renormalisation group flows in $d=d_c-\varepsilon$, with a potential and a metric regular at $\varepsilon=0$ up to logarithms of gauge couplings. We state properties of the renormalised functional with local couplings on the sphere $S^d$: finiteness, a local Weyl anomaly, the Ward identity of a conformal Killing vector, rotation properties and statements on the free theory. From them we derive a Ward identity without anomaly for a combination of the functional and its anomaly. Its first variation is a gradient formula whose symmetric metric contains the two-point function on the sphere and whose potential at fixed points is, in an extended form of the properties, proportional to the sphere free energy $\tilde F$ up to a constant. Sources of relevant operators enter through their Weyl variation, and in a scheme which we construct the gradient formula persists, with a nondegenerate metric if a matrix of the free theory is invertible. For multiscalar $\phi^4$ theory and for scalars and Dirac fermions with Yukawa and quartic couplings in $d=4-\varepsilon$, for sextic scalars in $d=3-\varepsilon$ and for cubic scalars in $d=6-\varepsilon$, we derive all these properties from a finiteness hypothesis. The gradient formula then holds to all orders for the beta function defined on the sphere. For interacting gauge theories the properties remain assumptions.
papers.summary: The authors derive a gradient formula for perturbative RG flows near critical dimensions using a renormalised functional on the sphere, showing that the metric is given by the sphere two-point function and the potential is proportional to the sphere free energy. They verify the formula for various scalar and Yukawa theories in dimensions close to four, three, and six, and discuss its extension to gauge theories.

papers.title: Near-boundary and near-horizon momentum--Krylov response in noncommutative-inspired BTZ spacetime
papers.authors: F. A. Brito, F. G. Costa, J. A. V. Campos
papers.abstract: We compute the proper radial momentum of a massive probe falling into a Lorentzian-smeared, noncommutative-inspired BTZ black hole at fixed asymptotic mass, and use it as the growth rate of momentum--Krylov complexity. In the BTZ limit the accumulated complexity is $\mathcal{K}_0 = X(\cosh\tau - 1)$. With smearing, the initial growth coefficient is $F'_\alpha(X)/4$, while the late-time exponent is the surface gravity $F'_\alpha(x_+)/2$. The two depend differently on the smearing parameter, so the deformed response is not a rescaled BTZ curve; we show this analytically and confirm it numerically. For a distant release point the early response approaches BTZ, whereas the late-time rate does not. A BTZ black hole with the same Hawking temperature reproduces the response to within about ten percent, and the remaining difference is set by the early/late mismatch. A Gaussian mass profile gives the same picture. The horizon radius and the surface gravity vanish at the critical smearing with exponents $1/2$ and $3/2$. At fixed mass the boundary stress tensor coincides with that of BTZ, but the $z^3$ Fefferman--Graham coefficient and the lengths of boundary-anchored geodesics do not.
papers.summary: The authors compute the proper radial momentum of a probe falling into a noncommutative‑inspired BTZ black hole and use it to study the growth of momentum–Krylov complexity, finding that smearing deforms the BTZ response in a nontrivial way. They show analytically and numerically that while the early‑time behavior approaches the BTZ limit, the late‑time growth is governed by the modified surface gravity, and the boundary stress tensor remains BTZ‑like but higher‑order Fefferman–Graham coefficients differ.

papers.title: Electromagnetic Memory as a Collider Observable
papers.authors: Felipe Diaz, Hern\'an A. Gonz\'alez, Oriana Labrin, Jakob Salzer
papers.abstract: Electromagnetic memory and charge correlators are measured by different detectors, sensitive to soft radiation and to hard charged tracks. We show that the Ward identity of large gauge symmetry relates these quantities as inclusive observables. For lepton pairs produced by an electromagnetic current, we compute all massless multipoint memory correlators and the massive two-point function, whose coincident limit gives the soft photon number. The correlators admit a celestial free-boson representation and remain finite at first radiative order, where recoil generates back-to-back Sudakov logarithms.
papers.summary: The paper shows that electromagnetic memory observables and hard charged track correlators are related by the Ward identity of large gauge symmetry, providing explicit multipoint memory correlators for lepton pair production and a massive two‑point function whose coincident limit yields the soft photon number. It further demonstrates that these correlators have a celestial free‑boson representation, remain finite at one‑loop order, and exhibit back‑to‑back Sudakov logarithms due to recoil.

papers.title: Tensionless M5-brane in light-cone gauge. The spinor moving frame method is wanted
papers.abstract: We perform the complete light-cone gauge fixing for the tensionless limit of the M-theory 5-brane the action for which was recently obtained in [1]. The problem of gauge fixing of local fermionic $\kappa$-symmetry becomes quite nontrivial because the projector of that is constructed from the gauge field strength which in its turn is required to be nonvanaishing and nontrivial in this limit. To resolve this problem the spinor moving frame method has been adapted. The corresponding moving frame is constructed on a vector quadratic in the gauge field strength, which is required to be nonvanishing and nondegenerate in the tensionless limit, and the derivative of the PST (Pasti-Sorokin-Tonin) scalar. The symmetries of the gauge fixed action and equations of motion are briefly discussed. To make a comparison with the case of usual tensionless p-branes (null-p-branes), those which do not carry worldvolume gauge fields, we also elaborate their spinor moving frame formulation.
papers.summary: The authors perform a complete light-cone gauge fixing of the tensionless M5-brane action, employing a spinor moving frame adapted to the nonvanishing worldvolume gauge field strength and the PST scalar. They analyze the resulting gauge-fixed action and equations of motion, and compare with the simpler null‑p‑brane case, highlighting the role of the moving frame in handling κ‑symmetry.

papers.title: Massive de Sitter correlators at one loop
papers.abstract: Fermions and massive fields charged under an unbroken symmetry couple to the inflaton only in pairs, so their signals in primordial correlators begin at one loop. Templates for these signals are mostly late-time estimates. Starting from a representation of massive de Sitter correlators as finite Mellin-Barnes integrals, we compute the exact squeezed coefficients of these signals and their corrections away from the squeezed limit. The leading coefficient factorizes into a hard part and a soft vertex. Late-time estimates treat the hard part exactly but approximate the soft vertex by its late-time limit, whereas we compute both exactly. Without a chemical potential, the exact coefficient differs from the late-time one by a universal factor that depends only on the masses in the loop and the coupling at the soft vertex. For the heavy Standard Model loops, the exact signals are ten to thirty times larger than their late-time estimates. With a chemical potential, the ratio depends on the model, and at our benchmarks it reaches a factor of thirty for helical vectors and about a hundred for the fermion triangle, where we agree with recent exact results. Away from the squeezed limit the leading term soon fails, mainly through a drift in the phase of the oscillation, which we derive for scalar and fermion loops.
papers.summary: This paper computes exact one-loop corrections to massive de Sitter correlators, providing precise squeezed-limit coefficients and corrections beyond the late-time approximation. The results show that heavy Standard Model loops can enhance signals by an order of magnitude, and the analysis includes chemical potential effects and phase drifts for scalar and fermion loops.

papers.title: Nonabelianization map for the $W_{3,c=2}$ conformal blocks. Part I
papers.abstract: This work is inspired by the nonabelianization construction of Virasoro conformal blocks. We start the process of defining the nonabelianization map which expresses $c=2$ $W_3$-algebra conformal blocks on a Riemann surface $C$ from Heisenberg blocks on a branched triple cover $\tilde{C}$ of $C$. This generalized nonabelianization map uses the datum of a $\mathfrak{gl}_3$ spectral network on $C$ and we find that this map also depends on the soliton degeneracies corresponding to the spectral network even though the soliton data didn't show up explicitly in the Virasoro case. This nonabelianization construction defines new formulas for $W_3$-algebra conformal blocks on $C$ in terms of fermion correlation functions determined by the Heisenberg blocks on $\tilde{C}$. We provide a check of the proposed construction associated to the more challenging $(123)$ type branch points which start to show up in three-fold covers. To be more precise, the simplest example that we focus on has only two of the $(123)$ type branch points and we show that in this example, our nonabelianization construction gives the desired two-point correlator and $\tau$-function.
papers.summary: This paper develops a nonabelianization map that rewrites $W_3$-algebra conformal blocks on a Riemann surface in terms of Heisenberg (fermionic) blocks on a branched triple cover, using a $mathfrak{gl}_3$ spectral network and soliton data. The authors test the construction on a two-point correlator involving $(123)$ branch points, confirming the expected $	au$-function behavior.

papers.title: A Minimal Toy Model of Charged Superradiant Spin-Down in Extreme-Mass-Ratio Inspirals
papers.abstract: Long-lived extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) are sensitive to slow changes in the mass and spin of their central black holes. We construct a deliberately minimal toy model in which an effective hidden charge opens a charged-superradiance channel, a bosonic cloud grows from a seed, and energy and angular momentum are transferred from a rotating black hole to the cloud. The model is not a Kerr-Newman perturbation calculation. Instead, it consists of a threshold function, one phenomenological rate coefficient, and balance equations that conserve the combined black-hole-cloud energy. This reduction yields an analytic relation between mass loss and spin-down and makes the roles of the growth coefficient, seed energy, and superradiant margin transparent. For an illustrative system with initial mass $2\times10^6 M_\odot$, spin 0.90, effective charge-to-mass ratio 0.30, and a one-year evolution time, the chosen benchmark reaches $M/M_0=0.8933$ and $a_\star=0.7704$. These values are then passed to FastEMRIWaveforms as two stationary Kerr snapshots. The resulting figures show that the endpoint state has a shifted time-domain oscillation pattern and a lower-frequency harmonic structure relative to the initial state. Because the snapshots are regenerated independently, they do not constitute a phase-connected, time-dependent waveform and cannot by themselves support a detectability claim. The value of the construction is instead diagnostic: it isolates a compact set of assumptions, exposes parameter degeneracies, and identifies the minimum ingredients required for a future self-consistent calculation. In this sense, the model provides a reproducible bridge between charged-superradiance intuition and EMRI waveform studies without presenting its benchmark as an astrophysical forecast.
papers.summary: This paper introduces a minimal toy model for charged superradiant spin-down in extreme-mass-ratio inspirals, linking black hole mass loss and spin-down via a phenomenological growth coefficient and seed energy. The model yields analytic relations and demonstrates how a bosonic cloud can alter EMRI waveforms, but it is not a full Kerr-Newman perturbation calculation.

papers.title: Spherical orbits around a Newman-Janis-generated rotating Bronnikov black hole
papers.abstract: We investigate spherical geodesics in a Newman--Janis-generated rotating regular geometry constructed from the magnetically-charged Bronnikov mass profile. The Kretschmann scalar is exponentially suppressed at the center, and is smooth across the disk and ring within the single-sheeted domain $r\geq0$. We show that all physically admissible spherical photon orbits outside the event horizon are radially unstable in the black-hole regime, whereas stable spherical photon orbits can exist in horizonless configurations. The unstable photon orbits determine the shadow, which for an edge-on observer is smaller and distorted compared with the Kerr shadow. For timelike motion, we identify marginally stable spherical orbits and determine the innermost stable spherical orbit (ISSO). We further examine the null, weak, strong, and dominant energy conditions, finding violations in the strong-field region but satisfaction of all four conditions asymptotically and throughout the exterior of every black-hole configuration. Together with stable causality and the curvature bound, these results show that the metric satisfies the five geometric criteria C1--C5 proposed by Maeda for physically reasonable nonsingular black holes.
papers.summary: This paper studies spherical photon and timelike orbits in a rotating regular black hole obtained via the Newman–Janis algorithm from the Bronnikov solution, showing that all admissible photon orbits outside the horizon are unstable while stable orbits exist only in horizonless cases. It also verifies energy conditions and geometric criteria, concluding the metric is a physically reasonable nonsingular black hole.

papers.title: Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity corrections in Dark Dimension scenario
papers.abstract: We investigate the thermodynamics, dynamical stability, and phenomenological implications of Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet (EGB) black holes in Dark Dimension scenarios with one or two micron-sized extra dimensions. For the asymptotically flat, neutral Boulware-Deser solution with positive Gauss-Bonnet coupling $\alpha$, we derive the mass, Hawking temperature, Wald entropy, and heat capacity in arbitrary dimension $D\ge 5$. A positive-heat-capacity branch arises only in $D=5$, where the temperature peaks at $T_{\max}=1/(8\pi\sqrt{\alpha})$ at $r_h=2\sqrt{\alpha}$ and vanishes in the zero-radius limit at finite mass $M_{\rm lim}=3\pi\alpha/(4G_5)$. For $G_5=(8\pi M_*^3)^{-1}$, $\alpha=M_*^{-2}$, and $M_*\sim 10^{10}$ GeV, this yields $M_{\rm lim}\simeq 1.06\times 10^{-12}$ g. While this branch formally overlaps with classical instability zones, the string ultraviolet cutoff safely suppresses the responsible high-harmonic modes. Assuming a UV completion stabilizes these relics, we show they can constitute all of cold dark matter. We map their observational signatures, highlighting a scalar-induced gravitational-wave peak at 33 THz and the suppression of Hawking bursts. In $D=6$, the heat capacity is negative at all radii. Within a bulk blackbody emission model, we derive the leading large-mass lifetime correction and the small-radius scaling $\tau\propto M_0^3$, compared to $\tau_{\rm GR}\propto M_0^{5/3}$. For $M_*\sim 10$ TeV, we identify distinct collider benchmarks: a steeper energy scaling for the production cross section and a suppressed decay multiplicity ($\langle N \rangle \sim 4$). These provide clear experimental signatures distinguishing 6D EGB gravity from classical General Relativity, mapping the transition toward the string scale.
papers.summary: This paper studies thermodynamic properties and stability of Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet black holes in a Dark Dimension scenario, deriving mass, temperature, entropy, and heat capacity in arbitrary dimensions and exploring relic dark matter candidates. It also predicts distinctive collider signatures and gravitational-wave signals that could distinguish 6D EGB gravity from classical GR.

papers.title: Imprints of perfect fluid dark matter distributions and topological defects on Born--Infeld AdS black hole signatures
papers.abstract: We construct a static, spherically symmetric \BI{} \AdS{} \BH{} that carries a topological defect, either a \GM{} or a \CS{}, and is immersed in \PFDM{}. The metric function collects four independent deformations of the Schwarzschild geometry: a constant solid-angle deficit $(1-\xi)$ from the defect, the nonlinear charge sector controlled by the \BI{} scale $\beta$, the logarithmic \PFDM{} term set by the intensity $\lambda$, and the \AdS{} curvature $\Lambda$. We verify that the solution reduces to the charged \AdS{}--\PFDM{} defect geometry as $\beta \to \infty$ and to Schwarzschild when all deformations switch off. The horizon, photon sphere, and shadow all grow monotonically with the defect strength $\xi$. We compute the innermost stable circular orbit and the epicyclic frequencies, read off the relativistic-precession predictions for twin-peak quasi-periodic oscillations, and confront them with five accreting sources through a Markov chain Monte Carlo fit. For spin-0 perturbations we obtain the scalar potential, the higher-order WKB \QNM{} spectrum, and the \GBF{}, all of which soften as $\xi$ rises. The extended phase space analysis yields a \VdW{}-type $P$--$V$ structure whose critical point shifts with the defect, the \BI{} scale, and the halo intensity. Throughout, the four sectors leave distinct imprints on imaging, timing, ringdown, and thermal channels, {\color{black} which we read as parameter sensitivities rather than as an observational separation of the four, a distinction a joint multichannel fit would be needed to settle}.
papers.summary: This paper constructs a static, spherically symmetric Born–Infeld AdS black hole with a topological defect and perfect fluid dark matter, deriving its horizon, photon sphere, shadow, and thermodynamic properties. It also studies quasinormal modes, epicyclic frequencies, and a Van der Waals–type phase transition, highlighting how the defect, Born–Infeld scale, and dark matter halo imprint observable signatures.

papers.title: ACT Excited: Reconciling Starobinsky and Quadratic Chaotic Inflationary Models with ACT Results via Excited States
papers.abstract: Data Release 6 of the Atacama Cosmology Telescope, combined with Planck, CMB lensing and DESI BAO data, favours a higher scalar spectral index $n_{s}$ than Planck and a mildly positive running $\alpha_{s}$, putting the Starobinsky model in tension with the data, while the quadratic chaotic model is already excluded by its large tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$. We show that relaxing the Bunch--Davies assumption for the initial state of the scalar perturbations can restore agreement without modifying the inflaton potential. Parametrising the Bogoliubov coefficients by an excitation parameter $\chi_{S}$ and a relative phase $2\varphi_{S}$, we derive the shifts of $n_{s}$ and $\alpha_{s}$ induced by their scale dependence and map the regions of the $(\varphi_{S},\chi_{S})$ plane compatible with the $1\sigma$ ACT DR6 ranges, the bound $r<0.038$, and the requirement that the scale of new physics $\Lambda$ exceed the Hubble scale $H$. For the Starobinsky model, a scale-dependent $\chi_{S}$ or $\varphi_{S}$ works almost everywhere in this plane: only small neighbourhoods of $\varphi_{S}=0,\pi$ with $\chi_{S}\gtrsim1.22$ are excluded, and a scale-dependent phase fails at $\varphi_{S}=0,\pi/2,\pi$ and at $\chi_{S}=0$, where the required ${\rm d}\varphi_{S}/{\rm d}\ln k$ and ${\rm d}^2\varphi_{S}/{\rm d}(\ln k)^2$ diverge. For the QC model, the excited state must also suppress $r$, which requires $\chi_{S}\gtrsim0.63$ and $\Lambda\lesssim6H$. A scale-dependent $\chi_{S}$ must satisfy $|{\rm d}\chi_{S}/{\rm d}\ln k|\gtrsim0.0021$ in both models, and in the QC model we show analytically that $0.0021\lesssim{\rm d}\chi_{S}/{\rm d}\ln k\lesssim0.0058$ and $0.0008\lesssim{\rm d}^2\chi_{S}/{\rm d}(\ln k)^2\lesssim0.0062$. If the tensor modes remain in the BD state, the scenario also predicts a violation of the consistency relation $r=-8n_{T}$, testable once the tensor power spectrum and its tilt are measured.
papers.summary: This work shows that allowing excited initial states for scalar perturbations can reconcile the Starobinsky and quadratic chaotic inflation models with the ACT DR6 data by shifting the spectral index and running, while keeping the tensor-to-scalar ratio below observational bounds. It maps the allowed Bogoliubov parameter space and predicts a violation of the standard consistency relation if tensors remain Bunch–Davies.

papers.title: Primordial black holes production in Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity
papers.authors: Ekaterina O. Pozdeeva, Sergey Yu. Vernov
papers.abstract: We consider models with the Gauss-Bonnet term multiplied to a function of the scalar field and propose a new inflationary model which provides a mechanism for the formation of primordial black holes (PBHs). For certain values of the model parameters, the predictions of this model agree with observational data from the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT). Due to estimation of possiable PBHs masses, we demonstrate that they can be considered as a possible source for all or part of dark matter.
papers.summary: The paper proposes an inflationary model in Einstein–Gauss–Bonnet gravity where a scalar‐dependent Gauss–Bonnet term enhances curvature perturbations, leading to primordial black hole formation that could account for dark matter. It shows that for specific parameter choices the model’s predictions align with ACT observations of the cosmic microwave background.

papers.title: Spin-Torsion Coupling: Vector and Scalar Torsional Potentials of Chiral Spinor Currents
papers.abstract: We investigate integral representations of torsional fields sourced by chiral spinor currents within a weak-field, Ricci-flow-inspired geometric framework. Starting from the coupling between spinorial currents and axial torsion, we construct screened Green-kernel solutions and examine their relation to antisymmetric tetradic perturbations and contorsion.   Particular attention is devoted to stationary toroidal configurations, for which the magnetic-type dipole moment vanishes while a nonzero toroidal moment and effective circulation remain. The dependence of these quantities on Yukawa screening is analyzed, together with their implications for an Aharonov-Bohm-like geometric structure.   We further introduce a mixed-chirality source describing an effective connection between oppositely polarized domains and investigate the corresponding flip-sector integral. The dynamics of massive Majorana neutrinos in an axial background is then examined, distinguishing chiral mixing from helicity oscillations and identifying the role of transverse torsional components.   The resulting framework connects spinorial sources, finite-range torsional potentials, toroidal geometry, and neutrino spin dynamics, while providing a mathematical basis for further investigations of torsional transport and observable effects.
papers.summary: The paper develops integral representations for torsional fields sourced by chiral spinor currents in a weak-field, Ricci-flow-inspired geometry, focusing on screened Green-kernel solutions and toroidal configurations. It also examines Majorana neutrino dynamics in axial backgrounds, distinguishing chiral mixing from helicity oscillations, and outlines implications for torsional transport and observable effects.

papers.title: Scotogenic dark matter from gauged $L_\mu+L_\tau$
papers.authors: J. Echeverria-Puentes, Sergey Kovalenko, Pablo San Martin Sartori, Carlos A. Vaquera-Araujo, Yoxara Villamizar, Jilberto Zamora Saa
papers.abstract: In this work, we introduce the first scotogenic model based on a gauged $L_{\mu} + L_{\tau}$ symmetry whose spontaneous breaking by two units leaves a remnant matter parity $M_P$. The resulting light active neutrinos are of Majorana nature and the lightest electrically neutral state mediating the scotogenic loop is stabilized by $M_P$ and can be identified as a weakly interacting massive particle dark matter candidate. We analyze the phenomenology of a predominantly singlet-like CP-even scalar dark matter candidate and the representative regions of parameter space compatible with the observed thermal relic abundance. The $Z'$ boson is compatible with a broad range of parameters relevant for dark matter. In particular, electroweak precision constraints do not lead to significant tensions for kinetic mixing values up to $\epsilon\sim 10^{-2}$. We discuss the implications of existing searches for leptophilic gauge bosons and the conditions under which visible and invisible collider signatures become relevant.
papers.summary: This paper proposes a scotogenic model with a gauged $L_{mu}+L_{	au}$ symmetry that yields Majorana neutrinos and a stable dark matter candidate via a remnant matter parity. It studies the phenomenology of a singlet-like scalar dark matter and a $Z'$ boson, including relic abundance, kinetic mixing constraints, and collider signatures.

papers.title: Chiral and deconfinement thermodynamics of the Polyakov-quark linear sigma model with and without charm quark: an SU(3) versus SU(4) comparison
papers.authors: Nourhan M. Rfeek (Assiut U.), Hossam Wahid (Assiut U.), Fatima M. Rfeek (Zewail City Sci. Technol., Giza), Alexandra Friesen (JINR), Yuri Kalinovsky (JINR), Saleh O. Allehabi (Islamic U. Madinah), Azzah A. Alshehri (Hafr El Batin U.), Ashraf F. El-Sherif (Ahram Canadian U.), Abdel Nasser Tawfik (Islamic U. Madinah)
papers.abstract: Using the Polyakov-loop extended linear-sigma model (PLSM), we investigate strongly interacting matter at finite temperature and baryon density by comparing the three-flavor (u,d,s) and four-flavor (u,d,s,c) formulations on equal footing, with the aim of isolating the thermal contribution of the charm quark. The model describes chiral dynamics through explicit and spontaneous symmetry breaking and reproduces the vacuum spectra of scalar and pseudoscalar mesons. Confinement is incorporated through a logarithmic Polyakov-loop potential calibrated to the continuum lattice-QCD equation of state (EoS). Within the mean-field approximation, we calculate light-, strange-, and charm-quark condensates, the Polyakov loop, and bulk thermodynamic observables, including pressure, trace anomaly, and entropy density, over broad ranges of temperature and baryon chemical potential. We also determine the chiral and deconfinement pseudocritical boundaries and represent them as phase boundaries and three-dimensional order-parameter surfaces. After tuning the Polyakov sector to lattice-QCD pressure and trace-anomaly data, the resulting entropy density agrees with HotQCD 2+1(+1)-flavor results throughout the crossover region. At zero baryon density, the non-strange condensate melts at Tc = 210 MeV in SU(3) and 218 MeV in SU(4), with curvature parameters kappa=0.018 and 0.017. Because mc>>Tc, charm remains thermally suppressed across the crossover. After normalization to the corresponding Stefan-Boltzmann limits, the SU(3) and SU(4) EoS nearly coincide below T~2Tc. Charm mainly contributes through a higher ideal-gas limit, a gradual high-temperature tail, and the flavor ordering u,d->s->c. For all baryon chemical potentials accessible within mean-field theory, the hadron-parton transition remains a smooth crossover.
papers.summary: This study extends the Polyakov-loop linear sigma model to include a charm quark, comparing SU(3) and SU(4) flavor sectors to assess the thermal impact of charm on chiral and deconfinement transitions. The authors calibrate the Polyakov potential to lattice QCD data and find that charm remains suppressed across the crossover, with the equation of state largely unchanged up to twice the critical temperature.

papers.title: Anti-de Sitter charges and maximal Cauchy hypersurfaces
papers.authors: A. Rod Gover, Jaros\l aw Kopi\'nski, Andrew Waldron
papers.abstract: We construct conserved charges of asymptotic symmetries for negative-cosmological-constant vacuum spacetimes from the Neumann data for the Hamiltonian and momentum constraints on maximal conformally-compact Cauchy hypersurfaces. This gives a general and canonical initial value treatment of charges for vacuum spacetimes with timelike conformal boundary.
papers.summary: The paper develops a canonical initial‑value construction of conserved charges associated with asymptotic symmetries in asymptotically AdS vacuum spacetimes, using the Neumann data of the Hamiltonian and momentum constraints on maximal conformally‑compact Cauchy hypersurfaces. This framework provides a systematic way to compute boundary charges that underlie the AdS/CFT correspondence and can be applied to study holographic Ward identities and boundary operator algebras.

papers.title: Unruh-like effects and correlation harvesting between particle detectors in uniform motion in (2+1)-dimensional Minkowski spacetime
papers.authors: Siwei Han, Zeinab Imani, Jun Feng, Robert B. Mann
papers.abstract: We study Gaussian-switched Unruh-DeWitt detectors coupled to a massless scalar field in the (2+1)-dimensional Minkowski vacuum and following four classes of uniformly accelerated trajectories: linear, catenary, cusped, and circular motion. We first determine how the single-detector transition probability and effective temperature depend on acceleration and the torsion-to-acceleration ratio $\bar{b}$, whose continuous variation connects these four trajectory classes. We find that both quantities generally increase with acceleration, while their dependence on $\bar{b}$ can become nonmonotonic depending on the energy gap.
