We also examine a correlation-harvesting protocol by two detectors following horizontally displaced copies of the same trajectory. Increasing acceleration or separation generally suppresses the harvested concurrence and quantum mutual information, but the extent of suppression at fixed acceleration depends strongly on the trajectory class. For each of the four trajectory classes, we identify regimes of genuine entanglement harvesting in which vacuum correlations alone suffice to entangle the detectors, while the communication contribution alone cannot overcome local noise.
papers.summary: The study analyzes how Gaussian‑switched Unruh‑DeWitt detectors coupled to a massless scalar field in 2+1 dimensional Minkowski space respond to four types of uniform acceleration, quantifying transition probabilities, effective temperatures, and entanglement harvesting between spatially separated detectors. It finds that acceleration and trajectory torsion generally enhance detector excitations and suppress harvested quantum correlations, with specific regimes where vacuum correlations alone can entangle detectors despite local noise.

papers.title: M\"obius Fusion Algebra
papers.abstract: Given a pseudo-unitary modular tensor category $\mathcal{C}$ with an anti-monoidal involution $\mathsf{P}$, we define a generally non-commutative algebra from this data, which we call the M\"obius fusion algebra $\mathfrak{M}$ of $(\mathcal{C},\mathsf{P})$, in terms of ribbon graphs drawn on the M\"obius band, where the orientation-reversal of the M\"obius band acts on the graphs by $\mathsf{P}$. We show that this algebra is semisimple, and give a formula for the dimensions of its simple modules, in terms of the modular $S$-matrix of $\mathcal{C}$ and a certain set of quantities extracted from the action of $\mathsf{P}$. This formula is expected to play the role of a non-orientable analogue of the Verlinde formula, in the context of Reshetikhin-Turaev-type topological quantum field theories on non-orientable manifolds.
papers.summary: This paper constructs a non‑commutative algebra from a modular tensor category equipped with an anti‑monoidal involution, using ribbon graphs drawn on a Möbius band. It proves the algebra is semisimple and gives a Verlinde‑type formula for the dimensions of its simple modules, extending the usual Verlinde formula to non‑orientable settings relevant to TQFTs.

papers.title: Thermodynamics of QCD+QED from the lattice
papers.authors: G. Endr\H{o}di, E. Garnacho-Velasco, G. Mark\'{o}, L. Peth\H{o}
papers.abstract: QED corrections to observables in QCD are by now well-understood at zero temperature, where QED effects are perturbative and required for precision physics observables, such as the neutron-proton mass difference or the muon anomalous magnetic moment, among many others. However, there are indications in the literature that at finite temperature the introduction of QED can lead to non-perturbative effects, affecting the structure of the phase diagram, since the combined theory is exactly center-symmetric. In this proceedings article, we analyze the structure of the combined theory and the different strategies to simulate it on the lattice, as well as presenting novel results of lattice QCD+QED simulations at finite temperature, focusing on understanding the role of the electromagnetic coupling in the thermodynamics of this system. We also discuss new features that arise in the combined theory and the challenges that these simulations entail, which require the development of new algorithms in order to understand the phase diagram of QCD+QED from first principles.
papers.summary: This proceedings article investigates the thermodynamics of QCD+QED at finite temperature using lattice simulations, highlighting how electromagnetic interactions can induce non-perturbative effects and alter the phase diagram. The authors present new simulation strategies and preliminary results, emphasizing the need for novel algorithms to capture the combined theory’s center symmetry.

papers.title: Compactification and non-zero density in (2+1)-dimensional four-fermion model
papers.authors: K. G. Klimenko, A. N. Kozhakin, R. N. Zhokhov
papers.abstract: The phase diagram of (2+1)-dimensional NJL type model has been studied with one compact dimension. The effect of compactification and fermion density on the chiral symmetry breaking is considered for periodic boundary conditions.
papers.summary: The paper studies the phase diagram of a (2+1)-dimensional Nambu–Jona-Lasinio model with one compact spatial dimension and finite fermion density, focusing on how compactification and chemical potential affect chiral symmetry breaking. The authors analyze the effective potential for periodic boundary conditions and map out the symmetry-breaking regions in the parameter space.

papers.title: Frobenius $2$-algebras and $R$-matrices
papers.abstract: In this paper, introducing Frobenius $2$-algebras, which are categorical generalizations of Frobenius algebras, we show that every Frobenius $2$-algebra determines an $R$-matrix satisfying the Yang-Baxter equation in the monoidal category of endomorphisms of its underlying object. Moreover, we illustrate this construction through three examples: a pair of objects in a braided monoidal category, a Hopf algebra with invertible antipode, and representations of the Heisenberg double of a finite-dimensional Hopf algebra. In particular, in the third example, we recover Kashaev's construction of the universal $R$-matrix. Thus, our construction provides a categorical generalization of Kashaev's construction.
papers.summary: This paper introduces Frobenius 2‑algebras, a categorical extension of Frobenius algebras, and shows how each such algebra yields an R‑matrix that satisfies the Yang–Baxter equation in the endomorphism category of its underlying object. The authors illustrate the construction with examples from braided monoidal categories, Hopf algebras, and the Heisenberg double, recovering Kashaev’s universal R‑matrix in the process.

papers.title: Void inside the horizon: connecting the third-quantized vacuum to a classical spacetime
papers.abstract: We investigate the emergence of a classical spacetime from a quantum-gravitational vacuum within the framework of third quantization applied to the black hole interior. Following the canonical quantization of the Kantowski--Sachs spacetime, one can construct a wave packet that explains the classical interior of a Schwarzschild black hole. This wave packet should be extended to the classical singularity. To avoid this, one can introduce an analytic continuation and the Euclidean wave function. This is not an analytic continuation of the spacetime, but of the superspace. To give this a suitable meaning, it is reasonable to introduce the concept of the third quantization. In this aspect, the Euclidean analytic continuation of the superspace explains the on-shell trajectory connecting the third-quantized vacuum state to a coherent classical geometry. Finally, we discuss how nonlinear self-interactions and baby-universe wormhole couplings must be incorporated into the third-quantized action to dynamically drive this transition.
papers.summary: This paper studies the emergence of a classical Schwarzschild interior from a third-quantized vacuum by constructing a wave packet in Kantowski–Sachs minisuperspace and extending it through a Euclidean analytic continuation of superspace. It then argues that nonlinear self-interactions and baby-universe wormhole couplings in the third-quantized action are required to drive the transition to a coherent classical geometry.

papers.title: Reconstructing Pure-State OTOCs from Forward-Time Linear Response
papers.authors: Yu-Hang Jin, Xudong He, Yu Chen
papers.abstract: We show that the connected out-of-time-ordered correlator (OTOC) of any pure state can be reconstructed exactly from commutator linear responses alone. The protocol requires no time reversal, no ancilla, no double copy, and no weak measurement: a unitary string pulse, forward many-body evolution, and a single local readout suffice. An average over a complete basis of pulse generators yields the OTOC exactly. We further show that the measurement can be made sparse by restricting the pulses to a fixed operator weight, which turns the truncation into an analytically controlled spectral filter: the deterministic bias can be computed before the experiment and cleanly separated from the statistical sampling variance. For Gaussian states, the finite-weight response is exactly proportional to the full OTOC after a known combinatorial rescaling. For quantum chaotic systems, the typical residual is suppressed as a power law in the sector size. Exact-diagonalization benchmarks in the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model and a nonintegrable Ising chain confirm these predictions.
papers.summary: This work shows that the connected out‑of‑time‑ordered correlator of any pure state can be reconstructed exactly from forward‑time linear response using only a unitary pulse and a single local readout, eliminating time reversal, ancilla, or weak measurement. The authors further prove that restricting pulses to a fixed operator weight yields a sparse, analytically controlled protocol, with exact results for Gaussian states and power‑law suppressed residuals in chaotic systems, confirmed by exact diagonalization in SYK and a nonintegrable Ising chain.

papers.title: Quark and gluon gravitational form factors of the nucleon at next-to-leading order
papers.abstract: We compute the quark and gluon gravitational form factors $A$, $J$ and $D$ of the nucleon in three-point QCD sum rules at next-to-leading order in $\alpha_s$ for the quark and gluon energy-momentum tensors (EMT), treating both at the same order in the $\overline{\rm MS}$ scheme. The nucleon EMT also tests the method, showing where the sum rules are reliable and why. Protected estimators of $D$ and of the trace form factor $\bar c$ require antisymmetric Borel moments, since none with equal Borel masses alone is protected. The $\mathcal{O}(\alpha_s)$ corrections reduce $A_{\rm tot}$ by $32$--$40\%$, $J_{\rm tot}$ by $22$--$27\%$ and $|D_{\rm tot}|$ by $21$--$27\%$, since the perturbative share of the two-point function is much larger. The total form factors agree with lattice QCD for $1\le Q^2\le2.5$~GeV$^2$. At $Q^2=1.5$~GeV$^2$, $A_{\rm tot}=0.337\pm0.113$, $J_{\rm tot}=0.206\pm0.100$ and $D_{\rm tot}=-0.206\pm0.121$. $D$ is the most reliable result: its correlator is mostly perturbative, and its quark and gluon parts agree with the lattice. In $A$ and $J$, a local gluon-condensate term that does not fall with $Q^2$ is the largest, and their gluon shares are well below the lattice, possibly because the gluon EMT couples at this order only through gluon exchange and the condensate. A working region exists only near $\beta=1$, and the constant part of transitions cannot be separated within the Borel windows. The individual conservation identities deviate at one point by two standard deviations, consistent with a missing finite term in the $g_{\mu\nu}$ structure, and $\bar c$ is therefore given at leading order with condensates.
papers.summary: The paper presents next-to-leading order QCD sum rule calculations of the nucleon’s quark and gluon gravitational form factors, comparing results with lattice QCD and highlighting the reliability of the $D$ form factor. It discusses the impact of perturbative corrections, condensate contributions, and the limitations of the method in extracting individual $A$ and $J$ components.

papers.title: Rank-Two Attractors and Modularity for a Mirror Bicubic
papers.abstract: We study the mirror family $\mathcal X_\lambda$ of the bicubic Calabi-Yau threefold, obtained from a family of complete intersections of two cubics in $\mathbb P^5$. We show that the four-dimensional weight-three Hodge structure of the fibers over $\lambda^6 = -8$ splits into two rational rank-two pieces of Hodge types $(1,0,0,1)$ and $(0,1,1,0)$; in particular, these points are rank-two attractor points. Using a Hesse pencil fiber-product realization, equivariant point counting, and the Serre-Faltings-Livne method, we identify their semisimplified $\ell$-adic Galois representations with those attached to the weight-four newform $f_{\mathsf{54.4.a.c}}$ and the Tate twist of the weight-two newform $f_{\mathsf{54.2.a.a}}$, where these labels refer to the L-functions and modular forms database.
papers.summary: The paper identifies special points in the moduli space of a mirror bicubic Calabi‑Yau where the weight‑three Hodge structure splits into two rank‑two pieces, corresponding to attractor points relevant for black‑hole physics. It further shows that the associated ℓ‑adic Galois representations match modular forms, linking the geometry to L‑functions and the Langlands program.

papers.title: The type-II double copy for relativistic Rindler fluids
papers.authors: Yu-Cheng Wang, Jing-Rui Zhang, Yun-Long Zhang
papers.abstract: Within the Weyl double copy framework, we study a mixed single-copy construction for the Petrov type-II geometry of first-order relativistic Rindler fluids. Working on a common fixed flat Rindler background with consistent spinor conventions and a real field strength representation, we algebraically factorize the Weyl spinor into two symmetric rank-two Maxwell spinors and test the Maxwell equations and the zeroth copy scalar equation up to the first order in the relativistic gradient expansion. We separate the degeneration parameter from the gradient expansion parameter and analyze the continuous degeneration to the Petrov type-D and type-N branches as the complex shear and vorticity tend to zero, together with the preservation of the accuracy of the Maxwell and scalar field equations along each path. We also compare the relativistic construction with the nonrelativistic case.
papers.summary: The paper extends the Weyl double copy to Petrov type‑II geometries describing first‑order relativistic Rindler fluids, factorizing the Weyl spinor into two Maxwell spinors and verifying the Maxwell and zeroth‑copy equations to first order in the gradient expansion. It also explores the degeneration to type‑D and type‑N limits and compares the relativistic construction with its nonrelativistic counterpart, offering insights relevant to fluid/gravity holography.

papers.title: A note on Kaluza-Klein theories
papers.abstract: We present a variant of the Kaluza-Klein theory that was introduced in previous papers (ATMP, 2020; LMP 2022; Ann. Fac. Sci. Toulouse, 2025), based on an action functional whose critical points, in the presence of point-wise constraints, lead-under reasonable assumptions-to the existence of a principal fiber bundle and solutions to the Einstein-Yang-Mills system. The difference is that it is not necessary to impose a point-wise constraint.
papers.summary: This paper proposes a new variant of Kaluza‑Klein theory that avoids point‑wise constraints by using an action functional whose critical points naturally yield a principal fiber bundle and solutions to the Einstein‑Yang‑Mills equations. The construction builds on earlier work but offers a more streamlined approach to unifying gravity with gauge fields.

papers.title: Imprints of quantum space in the ringdown phase of Kerr black holes
papers.authors: Nikola Herceg, Tajron Juri\'c, A. Naveena Kumara, Andjelo Samsarov, Ivica Smoli\'c, Kumar S. Gupta
papers.abstract: We investigate quantum-space corrections to the gravitational quasinormal modes (QNMs) of Kerr black holes within the framework of noncommutative geometry. The analysis employs a pseudo-semi-Killing Drinfeld twist, which preserves the classical Kerr geometry as an exact background solution while introducing nontrivial quantum corrections to linearized gravitational perturbations. Working to first order in the black hole spin and the quantum deformation parameter, including their mixed contribution, we derive a Schr\"odinger-like master equation for axial gravitational perturbations with a frequency- and spin-dependent effective potential. We compute the fundamental QNM frequencies using the WKB approximation and Leaver's continued-fraction method.Our results reveal corrections to the QNM oscillation frequencies and damping rates arising from rotation, pure quantum effects, and their interplay.To the best of our knowledge, this is the first systematic analysis of gravitational metric perturbations in a noncommutative Kerr black hole spacetime using a Drinfeld twist, extending prior work beyond the Schwarzschild case. Our findings demonstrate that quantum deformation effects alter both the oscillation frequencies and damping rates of quasinormal modes, with spin-quantum coupling introducing additional spin-dependent corrections to the Kerr QNM spectrum. Using a Kerr-anchored phenomenological prescription, we estimate the fractional frequency and damping-time shifts for selected merger remnants from the GWTC-3 and GWTC-5.0 catalogs. These estimates illustrate the potential signatures of quantum corrections in gravitational-wave ringdown.
papers.summary: The paper studies first-order quantum-space corrections to the axial quasinormal modes of Kerr black holes using a Drinfeld twist in noncommutative geometry. It finds that spin–quantum coupling modifies both oscillation frequencies and damping rates, offering potential signatures in gravitational-wave ringdown data.

papers.title: Dissipative Tidal Love Numbers of Neutron Stars from Viscous Heating
papers.abstract: We compute the leading low-frequency dissipative tidal response of nonrotating relativistic neutron stars. We formulate the response in a worldline effective field theory. We determine the linear dissipative Love number in two complementary ways: from the redshifted viscous entropy production inside the star and from the imaginary, frequency-odd part of the exterior metric. The first method reduces the calculation to an integral over the static equilibrium tide; the second provides an independent check. We apply our approach to publicly available equations of state and assess the corresponding correction to the gravitational-wave phase of neutron-star binaries. For an equal-mass $1.4+1.4M_\odot$ binary with both stars at a redshifted temperature $T_\infty=10^5\,\mathrm K$ and a standard electron shear viscosity, tidal dissipation shifts the gravitational-wave phase by less than $10^{-3}$ cycles between $20\,{\rm Hz}$ and $1\,{\rm kHz}$ for the four equations of state considered. Including the resulting rise in the stars' temperature in a simple thermal model reduces the shift below $10^{-6}$ cycles. For the viscosity model considered here, shear-viscous tidal dissipation in cold neutron stars is negligible for gravitational-wave phasing. This suggests that a measurable dissipative tidal signature would have to come from a different mechanism.
papers.summary: The authors compute the leading dissipative tidal response of nonrotating neutron stars using a worldline effective field theory, deriving the linear dissipative Love number from both entropy production and metric perturbations. They find that shear‑viscous tidal dissipation is negligible for gravitational‑wave phasing in cold neutron stars, implying that observable dissipative effects would require a different mechanism.

papers.title: Constraints on ultralight dark matter couplings from orbital perturbations of binary pulsars
papers.abstract: Ultralight dark matter coupled directly to ordinary matter perturbs the orbits of binary pulsars, and the perturbation grows secularly when its frequency matches a harmonic of the orbital motion. We use this effect to constrain three couplings with the wideband timing data for the $50$ binary pulsars of the NANOGrav 15 yr data set: a linear and a quadratic universal coupling of a scalar field to matter, and a vector field coupled to baryon minus lepton number ($B-L$). For every system and for masses between $10^{-23}$ and $10^{-18}\,$eV, we build the timing signature from the perturbed orbital elements. We then sample the coupling together with the local amplitude, phase and direction of the field and the red noise of the pulsar, marginalizing analytically over the timing model, and combine the single-pulsar likelihoods into $95\%$ credible upper limits at each mass. For a universal linear coupling, the orbital resonances of the eccentric systems bring the limit close to the Cassini bound. For the quadratic coupling, treating the neutron star as a point particle, the limits are the strongest available between $2\times10^{-22}$ and $2\times10^{-21}\,$eV. In the case of vector ultralight dark matter, the limit is comparable to the PPTA and E\"ot-Wash bounds between $3\times10^{-22}$ and $10^{-21}\,$eV and reaches or beats the E\"ot-Wash bound at isolated orbital resonances, while MICROSCOPE remains stronger over the entire mass range.
papers.summary: This study uses secular orbital perturbations of binary pulsars to set constraints on ultralight dark matter couplings, analyzing data from the NANOGrav 15‑year set across a range of masses. The resulting limits approach or surpass existing bounds for linear, quadratic, and vector couplings in specific mass windows, but the work is largely phenomenological and not directly linked to holography, celestial amplitudes, or related mathematical frameworks.

papers.title: Chiral crossover responses in a magnetic field: Finite-$\mu_5$ matching in the NJL model
papers.abstract: We investigate how independent information at finite chiral chemical potential $\mu_5$ constrains pseudocritical-temperature responses in the Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model under a magnetic field. Vacuum calibration alone leaves the coefficient $c_r$ of the additional interaction $\delta\Omega_r=c_r\mu_5^2(M-m_0)^2$ undetermined. We compare soft-cutoff (SC) and Pauli-Villars (PV) vacuum regularizations, each combined with the direct treatment (D) or the magnetic finite-difference scheme (MFDS). The reference SC and PV treatments exhibit opposite finite-$\mu_5$ responses already at $eB=0$. Matching the $eB=0$ scalar-susceptibility peak-temperature ratio predicted by unitarized chiral perturbation theory gives $c_{\mathrm{SC}}=-0.07112$ and $c_{\mathrm{PV}}=0.22479$. Holding these coefficients fixed at $eB=0.1,0.2,0.4$ GeV$^2$ reduces the four-treatment spread of the normalized finite-$\mu_5$-induced mass-inflection temperature change by factors of approximately $7.5$-$15.3$ at $\mu_5=0.15$ GeV and $18.1$-$32.6$ at $\mu_5=0.30$ GeV. For the distinct scalar-susceptibility peak-temperature ratio at $\mu_5=0.15$ GeV, the spread decreases by factors of approximately $74$, $27$, and $14$ at the same magnetic fields, respectively. The reduction in regularization-dependent finite-$\mu_5$ responses thus persists at the sampled nonzero magnetic fields without further matching.
papers.summary: This study refines the Nambu–Jona-Lasinio model by fixing an undetermined interaction term through matching to unitarized chiral perturbation theory, thereby reducing scheme dependence in the finite chiral chemical potential response under magnetic fields. The authors demonstrate that the calibrated coefficient stabilizes the pseudocritical temperature shifts across different regularization methods, offering a more reliable framework for exploring chiral crossover phenomena.

papers.title: Reproducing kernel and matrix representation of the deformed quantum optical density operator of $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$super-coherent states on $\mathcal{B}_0\oplus\mathcal{B}_1$ fermionic quantum algebra
papers.authors: Kaw\`eyim Lankpetre, Isiaka Aremua, Joseph D\'esir\'e Bukweli Kyemba, Bienvenu Gnim Adewi
papers.abstract: We study the $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$super-coherent states with two Grassmann variables $(\zeta_1,\zeta_2)$ built on the superalgebra $\mathcal{B}_0\oplus\mathcal{B}_1$ associated with the $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$deformed quantum algebras of Hounkonnou and Bukweli-Kyemba, the two dilation parameters $\phi_1(p,q)$ and $\phi_2(p,q)$ being meromorphic functions of two variables evaluated at $(p,q)$. The graded super-Fock space splits into four sectors: bosonic, $\phi_1-$fermionic, $\phi_2-$fermionic and bi-fermionic. In each of them we establish the diagonal representation of the density operator by means of the $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$derivative, angular integration and Berezin integration, and we give a unified compact form in terms of sectorial parametric functions. The total density operator is obtained in explicit form as the sum of the four sectorial contributions, and can be read as a mixture of the four sectors. We define the sectorial reproducing kernels, obtained from the resolution of the identity, we compute the matrix elements of the density operator in the super-coherent state basis, and we prove the hermiticity, positivity and matrix multiplication properties of the kernels, together with the series expansion of their diagonal values. An integral formulation relates the density operator, its density function and the reproducing kernel, the latter being the function associated with the identity operator. Berezin quantization in the bosonic sector yields the quantized operators associated with $z$, $\bar z$, $|z|^2$, $z^2$ and $\bar z^2$ and their mean values; the dispersions of the super-position and super-momentum operators show that the super-coherent states are intelligent states.
papers.summary: This work constructs a family of $mathcal{R}(p,q)$-deformed super‑coherent states on a graded fermionic algebra, derives their diagonal density‑operator representation in each sector, and establishes the associated reproducing kernels and Berezin quantization. The authors demonstrate that these states are intelligent with respect to the super‑position and super‑momentum operators, but the analysis remains within the realm of quantum optics and deformation theory rather than holography or scattering amplitudes.

papers.title: Central charges as black-hole hair in weakly coupled trace-anomaly gravity
papers.authors: Francisco Tello-Ortiz, A. V\'asquez, Kazuharu Bamba, Ghulam Mustafa
papers.abstract: We study black holes in Gabadadze's weakly coupled effective theory of the gravitational trace anomaly, keeping both the Euler and the Weyl central charges. We prove that a constant anomalyon on any Ricci-flat geometry, the Kerr family included, solves the full theory if and only if the two central charges coincide. Otherwise, the black holes continuously connected to this branch carry scalar hair whose charge is fixed by the surface gravity, the horizon topology and the difference of central charges alone: maximally supersymmetric matter leaves black holes bald, the Standard Model and photon-dominated sectors produce hair of definite sign, and conformal collider bounds confine it to a universal window. Electric charge separates the two anomaly invariants: the hair reverses sign at a critical charge-to-mass ratio set by the ratio of central charges, its extremal value retains only the Weyl charge, and the Euler charge governs the near-horizon growth of the anomalyon. For every unitary matter sector, the hair regular at the event horizon diverges at the Cauchy horizon. Finally, once the higher-derivative Weyl operator is order-reduced, the background, the anomalyon-graviton mixing and all propagation speeds depend only on the difference of central charges, which extends the no-ghost and Laplacian stability conditions to the full anomaly.
papers.summary: This paper investigates black holes in a weakly coupled effective theory of the gravitational trace anomaly, showing that constant anomaly solutions on Ricci-flat spacetimes exist only when the Euler and Weyl central charges coincide, and otherwise black holes acquire scalar hair determined by the difference of central charges and horizon properties. The analysis also demonstrates how the hair behaves under electric charge, its divergence at the Cauchy horizon, and how the theory’s stability conditions reduce to constraints on the central charge difference after order‑reduction of higher‑derivative terms.

papers.title: Fate of Vainshtein Screening for UV/IR Mixing with a $P(X)$ Higgs Classicalizer
papers.abstract: Classicalization is a non-Wilsonian framework in which an effective field theory self-completes above its strong-coupling scale by generating semiclassical objects that decay into many soft quanta, thereby realizing ultraviolet-infrared mixing. A key requirement of this mechanism is that the force carrier be lighter than the strong-coupling scale. A natural application would be to embed classicalization in the electroweak Higgs sector to address the little hierarchy problem. In this work, we investigate whether Higgs classicalization can occur within the $P(X)$ class of gauged k-essence and k-chameleon models. For classicalization to occur, the theory must support Vainshtein screening around a sharply localized source. Our results show that it fails to do so, even when one attempts to engineer a symbiosis with chameleon screening through a gauge kinetic function, owing to a strong-coupling breakdown inside the screening region. These $P(X)$ theories therefore fail to provide a suitable framework for Higgs classicalization. Nevertheless, we emphasize that our results, obtained for a specific class of models, should not be interpreted as a no-go theorem for Higgs classicalization.
papers.summary: The paper investigates whether Higgs classicalization can be realized in P(X) gauged k‑essence models, focusing on Vainshtein screening around localized sources. It concludes that such models fail to support screening due to strong‑coupling breakdown, ruling them out as a framework for Higgs classicalization, though not a general no‑go theorem.

papers.title: From joint attention to shared symbols: A free-energy principle account
papers.authors: Tadahiro Taniguchi, Koji Hashimoto, Ryuichiro Ishikawa
papers.abstract: Joint attention precedes vocabulary acquisition. How can attending to the same object help two people with different sensory experiences come to use a shared word? In a free-energy principle account, marginalizing the common object induces a statistical dependence between private perceptual states. In a categorical world, the joint prior inherits a mixture structure whose component index provides a candidate for shared reference. The collective predictive coding model approximates this prior by representing the dependence through that shared index. An established Metropolis-Hastings naming game lets agents infer and exchange words using private evidence. Toy and multiview image experiments illustrate how word exchange can coordinate private categories and improve the fit of collective models. The account connects joint attention to shared symbols through the coupling of private inference.
papers.summary: The paper proposes a free-energy principle framework linking joint attention to the emergence of shared symbols, modeling how two agents with distinct perceptual states can infer a common reference through a shared statistical index. It employs a collective predictive coding model and a Metropolis-Hastings naming game to demonstrate that exchanging words can align private categories and improve joint inference in toy and multiview image experiments.

papers.title: Multipartite entanglement structure of crystal quenches
papers.abstract: Understanding how entanglement emerges and spreads in out-of-equilibrium quantum many-body systems is a fundamental problem. In this paper, we investigate multipartite entanglement after quantum quenches. In particular, we study the entanglement structure and dynamics of quasiparticle multiplets generated by crystal quenches in the tight-binding chain. We identify zero-configurations for which a multiplet shared between three parties has no irreducible tripartite entanglement---these configurations consist entirely of pairwise distributed bipartite-entangled states. The existence of zero-configurations has important implications on the entanglement structure and dynamics of crystal quenches. For example, we show that it can further delay the production of tripartite entanglement. We build the quasiparticle picture for the Markov gap, and prove that it is a faithful witness of irreducible tripartite entanglement for crystal quenches. We discuss several key aspects of their tripartite entanglement dynamics through the lens of the Markov gap. We confront our results with exact lattice numerics and find perfect agreement in the hydrodynamic regime.
papers.summary: This paper studies how multipartite entanglement, specifically irreducible tripartite entanglement, emerges in crystal quenches of a tight-binding chain by analyzing quasiparticle multiplets and identifying zero-configurations that lack tripartite entanglement. The authors introduce the Markov gap as a faithful witness of such entanglement and confirm their predictions with exact lattice numerics in the hydrodynamic regime.

papers.title: Analytic $k$-essence Inflation
papers.abstract: In this work we develop a fully analytic $k$-essence inflation solution which is compatible with the observational constraints on inflation, without the need for the slow-roll assumption being imposed dynamically in the field equations. The analytic solution is obtained for a kinetic scalar sector of the form $K(X)= \frac{X^n}{X_s^{n-1}}$ and for the scalar field satisfying a tracking condition $\dot{\phi}^2=\gamma H^{-m}$. For this class of theories, the sound speed of the primordial curvature perturbations is constant, so no gradient instabilities occur in the theory. The Hubble rate, the scale factor and the scalar field can be analytically expressed as functions of the cosmic time, and the observational indices of inflation depend solely on the parameters $n$ and $m$. The resulting evolution is inflationary and it develops a pressure singularity a few $e$-foldings after the end of inflation. However, using qualitative and quantitative numerical arguments, we show that the pressure singularity is classically avoided when the matter fluids of radiation and cold dark matter are taken into account.
papers.summary: The authors construct an exact analytic solution for a k-essence inflationary model with a power-law kinetic term K(X)=X^n/X_s^{n-1} and a tracking scalar field satisfying δφ^2=γ H^{-m}. The solution yields constant sound speed, satisfies observational constraints, and predicts a pressure singularity that is avoided when radiation and cold dark matter are included.

papers.title: New analytic constraints for the soft anomalous dimension bootstrap at three loops
papers.authors: Einan Gardi, Luke Lippstreu, Andrew J. McLeod, Laura Walsh, Zehao Zhu, Enrico Zunino
papers.abstract: The soft anomalous dimension governs the universal long-distance singularities of gauge theory amplitudes. It exhibits a highly constrained analytic structure and has been shown to be amenable to bootstrap methods. In this paper we revisit the relation between unitarity cuts and sequential discontinuities of Feynman integrals and use it to derive new constraints on the soft anomalous dimension. At three loops, we show that certain sequential discontinuities in non-overlapping two-particle channels vanish for every web contributing to the quadrupole function that correlates four coloured partons. These constraints hold for arbitrary parton masses, and we explicitly verify them for the known massless and one-mass cases. We then demonstrate their constraining power by substantially strengthening the massless bootstrap and carrying out the first bootstrap construction of the one-mass quadrupole function. The new constraints are largely complementary to those arising from the absence of unphysical branch points, symmetries, and collinear and Regge limits. With their help, we determine each quadrupole function within the assumed function space up to a single coefficient, which we fix by matching to existing diagrammatic results. These results open the way to bootstrapping the three-loop soft anomalous dimension for amplitudes with several massive partons.
papers.summary: This paper derives new analytic constraints on the three‑loop soft anomalous dimension by studying sequential discontinuities in non‑overlapping two‑particle channels, enabling a bootstrap of the quadrupole function for both massless and one‑mass cases. The results significantly tighten the function space and fix the remaining coefficient using diagrammatic data, paving the way for future multi‑mass soft anomalous dimension calculations.
